_meta.note: Every number here is sourced from a committed results/*.json file, produced by a real, reproducible script run on the full 590,540-row IEEE-CIS dataset unless stated otherwise. Re-run any of the referenced scripts to reproduce.
_meta.hardware: GCP e2-standard-4 (4 vCPU, 16GB RAM), CPU-only, no GPU

graphsage_alone.note: underperforms XGBoost -- 5 epochs on CPU, undertrained relative to a fully-tuned baseline; see results/phase3_graph.md

xgboost_plus_graphsage_ensemble.note: naive rank-average is slightly WORSE than XGBoost alone -- honest finding, not hidden; root cause is unweighted ensembling of models of unequal quality (same failure mode as isolation_forest_ensemble below)

isolation_forest_ensemble.note: also worse than XGBoost alone -- IsolationForest's top-ranked anomalies had 0.0 precision@k at default hyperparameters

no_history_card_slice.note: new-card fraud rate is ~34% higher than overall -- a genuine independent finding; ensemble still doesn't beat XGBoost alone here either

serving.onnx_conversion_note: categorical-native XGBoost export genuinely fails (RecursionError / feature-name pattern error in onnxmltools); numeric ordinal-encoded serving variant works, documented in results/phase4_serving.md

load_test_50_users.note: p50 is 240ms under load vs 21ms single-request -- queueing from a single uvicorn worker, not slower inference

k3d_hpa_load_test.scale_trigger: cpu resource utilization above target (kubectl event, real)
k3d_hpa_load_test.probe_starvation_finding: near-simultaneous liveness/readiness probe failures across pods under 100-user load, one pod killed and restarted by kubelet
k3d_hpa_load_test.locust_failure_rate_caveat: 99.71% Locust failure rate during this test is a kubectl-port-forward single-pod-tunnel artifact, not a scorer-wide number -- see results/phase6_production.md

feast_materialize_vs_source.note: trivially consistent -- materialize is a straight copy, can't structurally diverge

real_time_redis_vs_buffered_parquet.root_cause: Parquet sink buffers 200 rows before flush (durability tradeoff) while Redis sink writes per-event -- online briefly ahead of offline, the reverse of the usual assumption
